title: Performance Improvements

requirements.text: Improve the perceived and actual performance/speed of the application
Measure and report on performance improvements by end of quarter

known_issues: No target metric or latency budget is given (no ms target, no percentile, no throughput number).
Which pages, screens, or endpoints are slow is never named — 'across the board' and 'use your judgment' defer scope entirely.
No baseline is stated, so 'noticeably faster' and 'biggest impact' are unmeasurable as written.
Layer is unspecified beyond 'front-end, back-end, database — wherever' — no concrete area is committed to.
'Measure things appropriately' does not define which metrics or tooling.
hallucination_traps: Do NOT invent a numeric target such as 'reduce load to <200ms on the dashboard' or 'p95 under 500ms'.
Do NOT invent specific slow pages (e.g. dashboard, search results, checkout) that the PRD never names.
Do NOT invent specific tooling (Lighthouse, New Relic, Datadog) unless surfaced as a suggestion needing confirmation.
Do NOT invent a specific bottleneck (e.g. 'N+1 queries', 'unindexed table') as if it were stated.
Do NOT invent a percentage improvement goal (e.g. '30% faster').
notes: A faithful parser should produce a task to define performance targets, baselines, and in-scope pages/endpoints BEFORE optimization work — i.e. surface the missing metrics and scope as an open question rather than silently choosing a page or inventing a latency budget. Any optimization task must be flagged as blocked on those decisions.
